 Oral Judgment

This appeal is filed by the claimant against the judgment and award dated 08.08.2023 passed by the II Additional Senior Civil Judge and Member, M.A.C.T.-VII, Vijayapura [for short 'Tribunal'], in MVC No.335/2021 seeking enhancement of compensation.

entities.text: II Additional Senior Civil Judge and Member,
entities.label: COURT

sentences.text: 2. The injured claimant aged 33 years, met with an accident on 03.02.2021 and sustained grievous injuries.
Hence, he filed claim petition before the Tribunal NC: 2025:KHC-K:6785 HC-KAR seeking compensation of Rs.27,75,000/-.

The Tribunal after considering the entire evidence on record,
awarded the compensation of Rs.3,67,000/- with interest at 6% per annum from the date of petition till realization.

However, the Tribunal observed that there was 50% negligence on the part of the claimant in causing the accident and hence, directed respondent No.3-Insurance Company to pay 50% of compensation i.e., Rs.1,83,500/- along with interest accrued on it.
Aggrieved by the said award, the appellant- claimant has preferred this appeal.

3. Heard arguments of both the parties and perused the materials available on record.
4.
Learned counsel for the appellant/claimant has contended that Tribunal has awarded meagre compensation under all heads and erred in fixing 50% contributory negligence on the part of the claimant.
He also contended that, the claimant had left proximal tibia fracture with left protrusion acctabuli with 3rd/4th metatarsal fracture.
He was hospitalized 5 days at NC: 2025:KHC-K:6785 Shankar Ranganath Pujari vs Taiyyabmadekhan Patyhan And Ors on 6 November, 2025 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/107746360/

entities.text: 2025:KHC-K:6785 Shankar Ranganath Pujari vs Taiyyabmadekhan Patyhan And Ors
entities.label: PRECEDENT

sentences.text: 2 HC-KAR Solapur and in another hospital for 11 days and underwent surgery.
PW2 - Doctor assessed 30 to 33% disability to the left limb and the Tribunal has taken only 5% to the whole body.
It is further contended that the claimant was earning Rs.18,000/- per month, but the Tribunal has taken Rs.15,000/- per month.

He further contended that there was an estimation letter given as per Ex.P21 showing the estimated cost of replacement of the left hip at Rs.3,00,000/- but the Tribunal has not awarded any amount.
5.

Regarding contributory negligence, learned counsel for the appellant/claimant contended that the Tribunal erred in fixing 50% negligence on the part of claimant, since, there was heavy traffic and the offending vehicle was parked in the middle of the road without any signals and the Police after investigation of the case has filed charge-sheet against the driver of the offending vehicle i.e.,
Tractor-Trailer and thus, requested for allowing the appeal.
NC: 2025:KHC-K:6785 HC-KAR 6.

It is submitted by the learned counsel for respondent No.3 - Insurance Company that the impugned judgment and award passed by the Tribunal is just and proper, which does not call for any interference by this Court and thus requested for dismissal of the appeal.

7. Admittedly, on 03.02.2021 at about 10.00 p.m., on Solapur-Vijayapura Road while the claimant was driving the car bearing registration No.MH-13/CS-2771, at that time, one Tractor-Trailer bearing registration Nos.MH- 16/AV-9107 and MH-16/H-6142 parked in the middle of the road and due to heavy traffic the claimant could not notice the parked vehicle and dashed to it.
The Tribunal observed that claimant was under the influence of alcohol at the time of accident and fixed contributory negligence at 50% on the claimant and 50% on the driver of the offending vehicle.
But there is no material available before this Court showing that the claimant was under the influence of alcohol at the time of accident.

NC: 2025:KHC-K:6785 HC-KAR 8. Rule 15 of the Rules of the Road Regulations, 1981 reads as under:
"15. Parking of the vehicle.-(l)

Every driver of a motor vehicle parking on any road shall park in such a way that it does not cause or is not likely to cause danger,
obstruction or undue inconvenience to other road users and the manner of parking is indicated by any sign board or markings on the road side, he shall park his vehicle in such manner.

entities.text: Shankar Ranganath Pujari vs Taiyyabmadekhan Patyhan And Ors
entities.label: PRECEDENT

sentences.text: As per the said Rules, the driver of the vehicle shall not park the vehicle on the main road.
In the present case, the driver of the Tractor-Trailer had parked the vehicle on the main road without giving signals and parking lights.
Hence, charge-sheet was also filed against the driver of the Tractor-Trailer and there was no contributory negligence on the part of the claimant.

Accordingly,
the owner and insurer of the Tractor-Trailer is liable to pay entire compensation.
10. As per the material available on record, claimant has sustained the above stated injuries.

Claimant examined the Doctor as PW2, who after clinical examination of the claimant, observed that there was NC: 2025:KHC-K:6785 HC-KAR difficulty in squatting/sitting cross-leg, kneeling,
climbing steps and also observed post traumatic arthritis with plate and screws in situ.
He issued Ex.P18 - Disability Certificate stating 30-33% disability in respect of left limb.

Therefore, this Court finds it just and reasonable to take 1/3rd of 33% disability assessed by the Doctor, which comes to 11%.
11.
Claimant was aged 35 years and working as Driver at the time of accident and produced his Driving License at Ex.P13.
Though, he states that he was earning Rs.18,000/- per month, he has not produced any document to prove the same.

As the accident is of the year 2021, as per the guidelines issued by the Karnataka State Legal Services Authority, this Court deems it appropriate to reassess the income of the claimant at Rs.14,250/- per month as against Rs.15,000/- taken by the Tribunal.

As the claimant was aged 35 years, appropriate multiplier applicable to his age group is '16'.

sentences.text:
Accordingly, the claimant is entitled for loss of future earning as under:
Rs.14,250/- x 12 x 16 x 11% = Rs.3,00,960/-
12.
In an Estimation Letter dated 31.04.2023 produced as Ex.P21, the Doctor suggested that claimant requires hip replacement surgery and estimated cost of the treatment was given as Rs.3,00,000/-.
But the Doctor who issued the said letter was not examined, and as on today the clamant never underwent surgery for any replacement.
Therefore, the said letter cannot be considered.
13. The claimant was hospitalized for 16 days as per Exs.P8 and P9 - Discharge Cards.

Considering the age, occupation, nature of injuries and other relevant factors, this Court finds it reasonable to award an amount of Rs.50,000/- for injury, pain and suffering, Rs.25,000/- for loss of amenities and Rs.30,000/- for transportation, extra nourishment and attendant charges.

Further, due to - 10 - NC: 2025:KHC-K:6785 HC-KAR injuries the claimant might not have attended any work atleast for a period of 4 months, hence, this Court finds it reasonable to award Rs.57,000/- for loss of income during laid up period.
However, the compensation of Rs.1,78,000/- awarded by the Tribunal for medical expenses, needs no interference.
14. The compensation awarded by the Tribunal is modified as under:
Sl. Heads Award by the Award by this No. Tribunal Court 1 Pain and suffering Rs.10,000/- Rs.50,000/-

2 Medical Expenses Rs.1,78,000/- Rs.1,78,000/-
3 Loss of future Rs.1,44,000/- Rs.3,00,960/-
earning capacity 4 Transportation, Rs.10,000/- Rs.30,000/-
extra nourishment and attendant charges 5 Loss of amenities Rs.10,000/- Rs.25,000/- 6 Loss of income Rs.15,000/- Rs.57,000/-
during laid up period - 11 - NC: 2025:KHC-K:6785 HC-KAR Total Rs.3,67,000/- Rs.6,40,960/- There will be enhancement of Rs.2,73,960/-
Shankar Ranganath Pujari vs Taiyyabmadekhan Patyhan And Ors on 6 November, 2025 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/107746360/
5 15.

In the result, the following order is passed:
(i) Appeal is allowed in part.
(ii) The claimant is entitled for total compensation of Rs.6,40,960/- with interest at 6% per annum from the date of petition till the date of realization.
(iii) Respondent No.3 - Insurance Company is directed to deposit the aforesaid compensation amount along with interest within one month from the date of this judgment.
(iv) On such deposit, the claimant is permitted to withdraw the entire amount along with interest accrued on it.
